slides.say: Given: x is equal to five a cubed minus five a, and a is a positive integer. x is necessarily divisible by:

So x is an expression with a cube, and they ask what always divides it. To see what always divides, we turn the expression into a product. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, factoring, and then plugging in a number.
[short pause] Let's start by factoring. Five a is in both terms, so take it out. Five a times, in brackets, a squared minus one.
at: Five a is in both terms

slides.say: And a squared minus one is the shortcut formula, a minus one, times a plus one. So x is five, times a minus one, times a, times a plus one.
at: a minus one, times a, times

slides.say: a minus one, a, and a plus one are three numbers in a row. And numbers in a row have a rule we haven't met yet. Let's build it.

Two numbers in a row, and one of them is always even, because even and odd take turns. Seven and eight, eight is even, so seven times eight, fifty-six, is even. Four and five, four is even, and four times five is twenty. So two in a row always divide by two.

Three in a row. Every third number divides by three, so one of the three does. And at least one is even. Two and three share no factor, so the product divides by six. Four times five times six is a hundred twenty, twenty sixes. Seven times eight times nine is five hundred four, eighty-four sixes.
at: Three in a row. Every third

slides.say: Now careful, only numbers in a row. Three times five skips a number, it's fifteen, and fifteen isn't even.
So x is five times three in a row, five times a multiple of six. It always divides by five times six, thirty. Choice number three is our answer.
at: Choice number three is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Now let's try plugging in a number. Careful, not a is one. Five minus five is zero, and zero divides by every choice, so it can't rule anything out.
So a is two. Two cubed is eight, five times eight is forty, five times two is ten, and forty minus ten is thirty.
Thirty doesn't divide by sixty, by forty or by twenty, so those three are out, and only choice number three is left. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
